It is the only Monster Prom voice with Vex's job: it speaks in the second person, already knows your worst habits, and lands on one humiliating concrete thing (Wilmer's Chicken Hut, a cattle prod). headToHead.voiceJudgement: Bar. With the names covered, about 8 of our 12 are clearly Vex. Five of them (the shed, the spoon, the shoes, finishing sentences, the mum skateboarding) are the receipt: a flat statement of your private life that stops on an object. That is a real sentence shape and it is hers. The other three (Married, monks, snorkel) give her away through words like Are You Still Watching, app and Users who followed, which tells you the topic, not the sentence. The kayak man, the bistro and 'I'm usually the list' could be Crumb or Tilly with one word changed. The Narrator is 12 of 12 from shape alone: 'You see', 'Later,', an ellipsis or a 'Wait,' followed by the deflation. Our gap on voice is smaller than in round 3. The danger now runs the other way: the rival lines are so uniform that they become a tell, a recognisable machine rather than a recognisable person.
headToHead.constructionJudgement: Tie. Line for line, ours is tighter. Every line is 19 words or fewer. 'Your neighbour's shed is just a shed' and 'step three is me' turn on their last two words and explain nothing, which is the bar's own trick. Two faults stop it beating the bar. First, the rhythm is one machine everywhere: a claim, a number or a place, the outcome, then a trailing fragment tag ('There's a ladle.', 'One sent a cardigan.', 'Crumb got custody.', 'Daily.', 'Twice, in slow motion.'). By the third line a viewer can time the punch. The bar varies length: a 26-word build into 'second-most dangerous day of school ever', then a six-word 'Later, you see Damien packing a bag.' Second, our nouns are still plausible (spoon, kayaks, soap, armchair) where the bar's are impossible (a boat made of bad vibes, a cattle prod for hair). Monks being shouted at and Goodbye, Egypt are the only two that reach the bar's size of leap.
headToHead.quotableJudgement: Bar, but closer. 'Married... Are You Still Watching', 'Goodbye, Egypt' and 'It now shouts at monks' would get clipped by people who have never seen the show. 'The shed is just a shed' would get screenshotted. The bar still has a higher ceiling. 'As cute as she was genocidal' and 'a boat made of bad vibes' get quoted as phrases on their own, while ours need the setup sentence before them to land.

templates: The dispatch machine, 21 lines: '[Name], I [show / put / file / forward / autoplay / match / subtitle] you [to someone / somewhere]. [Number of people]. [Outcome]. [Trailing fragment].' Round 3 asked for this and the writer did it everywhere. All 7 wingman lines open with fake praise ('Take Dash.', 'Tilly is wonderful.', 'Quill's very romantic.', 'Prince is a delight.', 'Crumb's a keeper.', 'Brock is so encouraging.'), and 6 of the 7 then give a headcount (eleven, nine hundred, a million, six, forty, forty). All 7 named jabs open '[Name], I'. Five of the six non-also-bought roasts open the same way. It is recognisably Vex, which helps the voice test. But in an episode where she roasts, wingmans and jabs, the audience hears the same four beats three times.
Haunt-your-feed after rejection, 6 lines: she will reappear in your feed, advert, sidebar or wedding. 'Me, but further away' is the best of these and should be the only one.
You secretly rewatch me, 6 lines: the star's data shows a private fixation on Vex. This is the same brag six times, and it is the vain version of the receipt, not the funny one.
Read the search bar aloud, 6 lines: a quoted embarrassing query. The receipt works better when it names an object ('a man restore a spoon') than a typed question.
'The [noun] one' as a closing tag, 5 lines.
Fake-praise label followed by evidence, 2 lines: 'Expensive taste, cheap checkout.' and 'Hard to impress, easy to predict.' are the same antithesis, and each states its point before showing it.

Number reuse: 'forty' appears five times (forty thousand phones, forty wedding lists, forty people, forty thousand couples, forty million people). Two roasts are set in the small hours (four a.m. for Dash, 2 a.m. for Crumb). There are three adverts (soup, gravy, holiday videos).
ruleBreaks: Mechanical: none. A script checked all 112 lines. The longest is 19 words, no opener is over 12 and no jab over 10. There are no em or en dashes, no exclamation marks, no emoji and no non-ASCII characters.

Persona rule 'do not open two lines the same way', broken five times: 'You're right. I'm sorry.' opens both q-fight lines. 'They cringed.' opens both afterCringe lines. 'They liked it.' opens both afterCharm lines. 'Understood.' opens or leads three lines (exit 1, exit 4 'Cut. Understood.', closeCold 1). 'Hello.' opens two (opener 5, ex-calls 2).

Persona rule 'never use the joke their own act already tells': 'Prince, I've marked you as spam. Out of respect.' Prince's own bank and Tilly's bank already make spam-folder jokes about him. 'Brock, I've subtitled you. It's all capitals.' is just his LOUD act restated. 'Tilly is wonderful... She's given every one a voucher.' is her free-upgrade act. 'Prince... He's paid every fee.' is his processing-fee act.
Cast collision: 'one lonely lighthouse keeper' in the Prince roast walks onto Vesper's signature prop. Her bank uses a lighthouse four times, including 'The lighthouse keeper would've wept'.
Stock romance filler, borderline: 'Alone at last.' (oneOnOne any 2) is a stock romance opener. The rest of that line saves it. 'is it everyone, or is it me' is a stock self-pity phrase.

Clarity: in '{rival} is the safe pick. They had a safe pick before. It was a beige sofa.' the second 'They' could mean the rival or the star. 'That's you, who sobbed at a gravy advert.' is broken grammar for the sake of a structure.
Real people and brands: none. 'Are You Still Watching', 'Skip Intro', 'Continue Watching' and 'Not Interested' are generic streaming-interface strings, and no brand is named. 'Egypt' is a country.
PG-13: clean. Therapy talk: none. The weighted blanket is a product, not therapy language. 'As an AI': none. Lists: none. The 'Thursday, dishwasher, bowls' tricolon is one sentence and passes.

Too nice: not applicable. This is a suitor bank, with no star reactions or cuts. The one soft line, 'For once, I won't finish your sentence. Go on. You say it.', says the persona's want out loud, which the persona forbids.
biggestGap: Her rhythm has become one machine: a claim, a headcount or place, the outcome, then a trailing fragment tag after the joke has already landed ('There's a ladle.', 'Daily.', 'One sent a cardigan.', 'Twice, in slow motion.'). It runs through all 21 rival lines and most of the rest, so a viewer can time the punch before it comes. In the next pass, rewrite at least half the bank as one unbroken sentence that turns once on its final noun, with 'Your neighbour's shed is just a shed' and 'Users who followed Nav also bought a snorkel' as the models. Cut every fragment that follows the laugh, and take the number out of the wingman lines.

notes: I read monster-prom-lines.md in full, including the voice section, plus charm-notes.md, CAST.md, the persona, the types.ts comments and all 112 bank lines. A script checked word limits and banned characters, and I grepped the other banks for prop collisions. The bank has been heavily rewritten since round 3. Round 3's biggest gap, rivals' secrets read aloud, is fixed: no rival line spends a CAST.md secret except the snorkel's nod to Nav's lake, which is indirect and earns it. The 'You liked X once' misfire template is gone, and the misfires are now mostly the ad for herself, as asked. The generic share is 53% (59 of 112 lines, each counted once). That is up from 39%, but only because the dispatch frame now fills all 21 rival slots. Without the dispatch lines it is 38 of 112, or 34%, which is an improvement. Many of the dispatch lines are good (monks, custody, ladle, sleep clinic, leeches, the clown), so the fix is varying their shape, not cutting them. Protect these as well: the spoon, lasagne step three, the shoes, 'I finish your sentences. By week two you'll stop starting them.', the mum skateboarding, 'You saved the lilac', 'Five stars for this evening. I posted the review this morning.', and 'I've gone all spinning wheel'. Outside this bank: quill.json's Vex roast ('I asked her mine. She said goats.') spends Vex's on-stage secret, which her persona forbids hinting at on stage. Fix it in Quill's file.
